# Metaplate v0.7.0

Metaplate 0.7 makes deployed social images verifiable end to end: the bytes a route serves, the metadata a page publishes, the headers a provider forwards, and the dependency tree behind the package are now checked by the same executable contracts, locally and in CI.

> **Upgrade recommendation:** Recommended for every 0.6 user. Callers who configure `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Encoding`, or `ETag` through `headers` on `createNodeOg`, or who pass a custom `output.contentType`, must review the breaking changes below.

## Why upgrade

Deploying an Open Graph route used to mean trusting that the image a function rendered matched the descriptor the page advertised and that the provider did not rewrite the response. Version 0.7 turns those assumptions into checks. `verifySocialImage` verifies encoded bytes against the published descriptor and the platform profiles in one report, `artifact()` returns bytes and metadata from the same copy so they cannot drift, and Node responses own their representation headers and can carry deterministic strong ETags.

The release also adds provider-neutral Fetchable route handlers, corrects the Vercel and Netlify examples against their documented conventions, verifies GIF files structurally, and ships an auditable supply-chain baseline: a dependency inventory derived from the lockfile, a Socket score artifact with dispositions for every high or critical alert, pinned CI actions, and release evidence bound to the commit that produced it.

## Highlights

### One verification contract for bytes and metadata

- `verifySocialImage(bytes, descriptor, { targets, maxFileSize })` from the root entry checks dimensions, media type, byte length, and every selected compatibility profile together. Structural image failures still throw; metadata and compatibility findings are returned for CI reporting.
- `metaplate verify` gains `--json` for one stable report per file, repeatable `--target` profiles, `--url` and `--alt` descriptor fields, `--max-file-size`, and `--format gif`. File-level validity is reported separately from per-target compatibility, and metadata flags are rejected without a target rather than silently ignored.
- GIF87a and GIF89a files are walked block by block: global and local color tables, graphic control, application, comment, and plain-text extensions, image data sub-blocks, and the trailer.
- `socialImageCompatibility` accepts descriptors without a URL or alt text through `checkUrl`/`checkAlt`, and LinkedIn checks warn when an image drifts from the documented 1.91:1 aspect ratio.

### Deployment contracts that match provider conventions

- `fetchable(copy)` and `fetchableFrom(resolve)` on both `createNodeOg` and `createNextOg` return the `{ fetch }` shape that Fetch-style providers consume directly. See the [deployment routes guide](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.7.0/docs/deployment.md), which now ships in the npm package.
- The Vercel example consumes a Web `Request` per the [Vercel Node.js runtime reference](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/node-js); the Netlify example reads `params` from the second `context` argument per the [Netlify Functions configuration reference](https://docs.netlify.com/build/functions/configuration/). Both forms, plus an Express service in the shape [Railway documents](https://docs.railway.com/guides/express), are exercised against the packed tarball, rendering two slugs per route to prove the request reached the copy resolver.
- `artifact(route, copy)` returns bytes, byte length, format, content type, dimensions, descriptor metadata, and an optional ETag from one render.
- Node responses now set `Content-Length`, never set `Content-Encoding`, and with `etag: "sha256"` (or `etag: true`) carry a strong ETag computed from the final encoded bytes.
- Edge runtimes remain explicitly unsupported for the native renderer, and hosted provider certification is not claimed: the shipped evidence is local packed-contract evidence only.

### Reliability and safety

- Empty custom encoder output and syntactically invalid custom media types fail at definition or render time instead of becoming HTTP responses.
- `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, and `Content-Encoding` can no longer be configured through `headers`; previously a caller `Content-Type` was silently overwritten.
- The CLI usage line, README, and CHANGELOG document every new flag and export.

### Supply-chain and release evidence

- `npm run check:dependencies` derives a reachability inventory from `package-lock.json` (regular, peer, optional-peer, optional, and development edges), requires every package to resolve to the npm registry with a sha512 integrity, forbids git, URL, and file dependencies, and takes `hasInstallScript` only from the lockfile so the inventory is identical on every platform. The published runtime dependency count is zero.
- The official Socket baseline for `metaplate@0.6.0` is committed as a hash-bound score artifact. Every high or critical alert must match exactly one disposition by type, package, version, and dependency path; critical alerts block release. The single high alert (a maintenance upgrade signal in a transitive Satori dependency) is an expiring, evidence-backed exception.
- `npm run check:workflows` requires every GitHub Actions reference to be pinned to a full commit SHA, and CI runs `npm audit signatures` so every installed package carries a valid registry signature and, where published with provenance, a verifiable attestation.
- `npm run release:evidence` re-runs the build, packed-artifact, inventory, deployment, Socket, and workflow checks, records each result with captured output, and writes a report bound to the commit and version. CI retains the bundle even when a check fails, and the bundle verifier rejects failed, foreign, or incomplete reports.

## Breaking changes

- `createNodeOg` throws a `TypeError` at definition time when `headers` contains `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, or `Content-Encoding`, or contains `ETag` while automatic `etag` generation is enabled. Remove those headers; Metaplate sets the first two itself and never sets encoding. A caller `ETag` still passes through when `etag` is off.
- A custom `output.contentType` must be a syntactically valid media type.
- `socialImageCompatibility` throws a `TypeError` when the descriptor lacks `width` or `height`.

## Install or upgrade

```sh
npm install metaplate@0.7.0
```

That single command includes the framework-neutral SVG and PNG renderer. Next
applications continue to supply their own compatible `next` dependency.

## Verification

- `npm run check` passes lint, a zero-tolerance duplication scan, workflow pin policy, dependency inventory and Socket disposition policy, deployment evidence policy, release-note validation, source and example type checks, 377 tests, build, and a 34-file package dry run.
- `npm run check:package` passes against the exact local tarball: lean and standalone consumers, offline Next static export, Astro static build, Express service, React Router resource route, and the Vercel `handlerFrom`, Vercel Fetchable, and Netlify `context.params` deployment fixtures with image and response-header evidence.
- `npm run release:evidence` records six passed release checks and a verified evidence bundle; CI uploads the bundle on every run.
- The Socket score artifact is historical `0.6.0` evidence captured on 2026-08-25 and is not presented as a fresh scan of this release; refreshing it requires an authenticated Socket export.
- npm registry signature and SLSA provenance verification run automatically after publication and remain the final release check because they cannot execute before the public artifact exists.
